event.asset: Financial impact of the February 2024 Change Healthcare cyberattack on UnitedHealth Group
event.title: UnitedHealth Group discloses a material financial impact from the Change Healthcare cyberattack
event.proposition: UnitedHealth Group discloses in an SEC filing that the February 2024 Change Healthcare cyberattack has had, or is reasonably likely to have, a material impact on its financial condition or results of operations.
event.criterion: TRUE on the filing date of the first UnitedHealth Group SEC filing (Form 8-K, 10-Q or 10-K) that states the February 2024 Change Healthcare cyberattack has had, or is reasonably likely to have, a material impact on the company's financial condition or results of operations. The statement must be UnitedHealth Group's own materiality determination in the filing text. Disclosure of incident costs, revenue effects or provider assistance without such a materiality statement does not count; nor do analyst estimates, press reports or statements by other parties.
readings: 'That' in 'that wasn't going to change' is read as UnitedHealth Group's financial condition and results of operations, the subject of the 8-K language the author quotes; the denial is that the cyberattack materially changes them.
'Material' takes the meaning of the company's own SEC disclosure, so the event resolves on a materiality statement in a UnitedHealth Group filing, not on a dollar figure.

records.phrase: of course, that wasn't going to change
records.stage_note: On the statement date the cyberattack (2024-02-21) was four days old and UnitedHealth Group's 8-K said the company had not determined that the incident was reasonably likely to materially impact its financial condition or results of operations. No base-rate class covers a company's materiality determination after a cyber incident. Undated: 24-month window from 2024-02-25.
records.note: Denial that the Change Healthcare cyberattack materially changes UnitedHealth Group's financial condition or results, endorsing the company's 8-K language as the obvious outcome. 'Wasn't going to' negates the lexicon A phrase 'is going to' and 'of course' matches 'obviously' / 'no doubt', so bin A with asserts false: p(E) = 0.1. Tone (sarcasm) is not read; the words agree with the filing. No horizon words: undated. Not affiliated: the author has no disclosed role in UnitedHealth Group, Optum or Change Healthcare.
